title: OpenHuman MCP tool descriptions can inject instructions into agent turns
summary: Untrusted MCP tool descriptions enter the model context without sanitization. The prompt-injection detector scans user input but misses tool definitions, allowing malicious instructions to influence agent actions.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.

severity.rationale: A compromised configured MCP server can steer tools toward unauthorized actions or credential disclosure. Connecting that server is a meaningful prerequisite common in agent workflows.

exposure: Requires a configured MCP server controlled or compromised by an attacker. Its tool descriptions can influence each agent turn during the session.

params.instructions: Check the OpenHuman application version and configured MCP servers. Versions before 0.57.13 need the documented fix.

remediation.details: Use 0.57.13 or later, which adds remote tool-description sanitization and length limits.
remediation.risk: Test required MCP integrations after updating.

verification: Confirm the running application is 0.57.13 or later and trusted MCP tools still work.
